questions.stem: A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {x, y}. How many ordered pairs (a, b) with a in A and b in B are there?
questions.explain: Each of the 3 choices for a pairs with each of the 2 choices for b: 3 × 2 = 6 pairs.

questions.stem: R = {(a, 1), (a, 2), (b, 2)} is a set of pairs. How many different second values are paired with a?
questions.explain: The pairs starting with a are (a, 1) and (a, 2), so a is paired with 1 and 2.

questions.stem: 30 students take course X, 20 take course Y, and 10 take both. How many students take at least one of the two?
questions.explain: Add the two groups and subtract the overlap that was counted twice: 30 + 20 − 10 = 40.

questions.stem: Which formula says "every employee works in some department"?
questions.explain: Each employee e gets their own department d, so ∀e comes first. ∃d ∀e would force one department to hold all employees.

questions.stem: How many non-empty subsets does the set {x, y, z} have?
questions.explain: A 3-element set has 2³ = 8 subsets, and removing the empty one leaves 7.
